approved: Tertiary Education Legislation Amendment (There For Education, Not Profit) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would cap the pay of Australian university vice-chancellors at $430,000 a year.

It would amend the Australian National University Act 1991 to apply the cap to the Australian National University and the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency Act 2011 to require other public universities to comply.

The Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (TEQSA) could obtain information from universities about vice-chancellor pay, and the minister could prescribe a different amount by legislative instrument subject to parliamentary disallowance.
Sets a statutory limit of $430,000 on vice-chancellor remuneration.
Empowers TEQSA to obtain information from universities about vice-chancellor pay.
Allows the minister to prescribe a different amount by legislative instrument, which must be made before 1 July of the preceding year to take effect.
Australian public universities and their vice-chancellors, particularly the Australian National University.

Moved to restore the Tertiary Education Legislation Amendment (There For Education, Not Profit) Bill 2025, the Remuneration Tribunal Amendment (There For Public Service, Not Profit) Bill 2025 and the Whistleblower Protection Authority Bill 2025 to the Notice Paper, resume second reading consideration and refer them to committees for inquiry and report; each question was agreed to.
